precepts.text: We see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death. Before that, in Exodus, he did not come a little lower than the angels. It became him to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings: the captain of our salvation is the captain of the Lord's host that we read about with Joshua.
precepts.point: And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come. Who is the captain of the host of the Lord? This is talking about Christ.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
By Jericho, Joshua saw a man standing over against him “with his sword drawn in his hand”, and Joshua stepped to him: “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?” You for me or for my enemies? Let me know. And he answered, “Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Who is the captain of the host of the Lord? This is talking about Christ, and Hebrews shows it.

“But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.” He came down a little lower than the angels when he came the last time. Before that, in Exodus, he did not come a little lower than the angels; he came down like an angel. That is how he stood before Joshua with his sword drawn.

“For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect”. The captain of our salvation is the captain of the host of the Lord, the Lord of armies, that we read about with Joshua in Joshua 5. That was Christ who was there.

This is the book of the wars of the Lord. The same Christ who led the host when Israel came out of Egypt and conquered the land, and who is the captain of our salvation, is the one who fights for Israel. Joshua fell on his face and worshipped him, because the battle is the Lord's.

precepts.text: The captain of the host of the LORD said to Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy; the same command given at the bush.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
At the bush the voice said, “put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.” When Joshua was by Jericho, “there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand”, who said, “as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Joshua fell on his face and worshipped, and “the captain of the Lord’s host said unto Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy.”

It is the same command that was given at the bush, from the same one. The captain of the host of the Lord is the angel that appeared to Moses in the flame of fire, and Hebrews 2 names the captain: Christ.

precepts.text: The covenant with Abraham and his seed: every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, including the servant bought with money.
precepts.point: When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Joshua to “circumcise again the children of Israel the second time.” Circumcision is the covenant the Most High instituted with our forefather Abraham: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.” It is “a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.” Every man child circumcised at eight days old, and the servant “born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger” circumcised likewise and keeping the laws as well.

The eighth day is the wisdom of the Most High for the body: before then a baby's blood has not begun to coagulate as it needs to, and the child could bleed out; by the eighth day he is strong enough to withstand the process and heal.

There are physical benefits to the law: when the foreskin remains, moisture gets trapped and creates an environment for bacteria, raising the risk of infection and urinary tract infections, and being circumcised even reduces a wife's risk of cervical cancer. This is the Most High as a Father giving his children counsel on how to live and stay clear of disease. The children of Israel in Joshua's day had not been keeping the commandments, being stiffnecked and hardheaded, and the Lord told Joshua to fix them.

precepts.text: Abraham circumcised every male of his house in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him; faith shown by doing.
precepts.point: When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
When Abraham received the commandment he performed it: “And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house; and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.” He himself was ninety years old and nine.

The selfsame day: he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed, faith shown by doing. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision, the way Abraham did.

precepts.text: If then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they accept the punishment of their iniquity; the Lord speaks here of the heart, not the flesh.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
The physical circumcision is symbolic of spiritual circumcision. The Lord speaks here of the heart, not the flesh: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”. He has walked contrary unto them and brought them into the land of their enemies, and what has to be humbled is the uncircumcised heart.

The uncircumcised heart is the mind that will not keep the commandments. That is what the second circumcision in Joshua points to: not only the flesh, but the heart.

precepts.text: From within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts; the heart is the mind.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
The heart in scripture is the mind: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders”. Evil thoughts proceed from the heart, so the heart is the mind.

Sin is what makes a man dirty, nasty, and filthy, so the uncircumcised heart is the mind that will not keep the commandments. The uncircumcised heart of Leviticus 26 is the mind these things proceed from.

precepts.text: Wash you, make you clean; cease to do evil is how you are made clean.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil”. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil.

That is the spiritual circumcision the flesh points to. The men of Joshua's day applied the law of circumcision as a form of repentance; the heart is circumcised by putting away the evil of your doings.

precepts.text: A young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” A young man cleanses his way by taking heed to it according to the word of the Most High.

That is the circumcision of the heart: no surgery, but repentance, ceasing to do evil and taking heed to your way by the word. The flesh was circumcised at the hill of the foreskins; the mind is circumcised by the word.

precepts.text: The rebels called the land Israel came out of a land that floweth with milk and honey; that land was Egypt.
precepts.point: The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“a land that floweth with milk and honey.” The Bible's own dictionary, precept upon precept, tells what that means. The rebels said to Moses, “Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land that floweth with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness”. The land they were brought up out of was Egypt; so the rebels called Egypt the land flowing with milk and honey.

So the phrase describes a land abundant in food. The milk goes into your cattle and your meats, and the honey goes into your vegetation.

precepts.text: I am the Lord thy God which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
precepts.point: The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” This settles which land the rebels in Numbers 16 called the land flowing with milk and honey: Israel was brought out of the land of Egypt.

So Egypt was called a land that floweth with milk and honey, and it was also the house of bondage. The phrase means a land abundant in food, milk in the cattle and meats, honey in the vegetation; and the land the Lord sware to give us is that kind of land.

precepts.text: The mixed multitude fell a lusting, and Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic of Egypt; comfortable in their oppression.
precepts.point: The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”.

That is the milk and honey of Egypt, the food they wept for. They were comfortable in their oppression and did not understand they were not free, in the house of bondage crying for its fish and cucumbers. It is the same mindset among our people in captivity today who say they are free and living their best life. These are the men of war who obeyed not the voice of the Lord and were consumed in the wilderness.

precepts.text: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee; the honey goes into your food, and the lesson is moderation.
precepts.point: The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: “Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.” The honey goes into your food, your vegetation, and the lesson is moderation.

Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately. Even in a land that floweth with milk and honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee.

precepts.text: We see Jesus, made perfect through sufferings, the captain of their salvation; Christ is the captain of the host.
precepts.point: The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Host means army: he is the captain, the leader, of the army of the Lord. And who is that captain? “But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour”, and it became him, in bringing many sons unto glory, “to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.”

The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. That is why Joshua, who had no fear walking up to a man with his sword drawn, fell on his face to the earth and did worship when he realized who stood before him, and the leader of Israel's army called himself a servant: “What saith my lord unto his servant?” Joshua had cleaved to Moses and understood who the captain of the host is.

precepts.text: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man; at his second coming Christ comes with the power of the living God.
precepts.point: The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
Joshua was afraid of the captain of the host, and he had reason. “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” The return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints. He is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy.

I will not meet thee as a man: no missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him. The man with his sword drawn by Jericho is that same captain.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.
precepts.point: The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The one Joshua saw was a warrior, a man with his sword drawn in his hand, and he came as captain of the host of the Lord. That is who the Lord is: a man of war.

So the captain of the army of the Lord standing over against Joshua by Jericho was no soft figure. He is a man of war, and Joshua fell on his face.

The children of Israel finally sanctified themselves, and the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day.
